text:
marta: Heads up — saw a small eviction churn cluster-wide after the autoscaler added 30 nodes in us-east1 about 03:10 UTC. Looks like the slot rebalancer hit its global rate limit and started queueing drains, which then spilled into aggressive preemption once pending pods aged out.

tyler: pinged the metrics, can you paste the rebalancer logs?

marta: here are the last 20 lines from the rebalancer during the window:
```
[03:09:54] rebalancer INFO acquire-token failed: tokens=0 throttle=global_rate_limit
[03:09:55] rebalancer WARN enqueue drain pod/prefix-123 on node/gpu-45
[03:09:58] scheduler INFO preempt pod/model-train-9 due to pending timeout
[03:10:02] rebalancer INFO tokens replenished=5
[03:10:03] rebalancer INFO processed 2 drains, backlog=28
[03:10:10] rebalancer ERROR failed to sync node/gpu-90: context deadline exceeded
```

kevin: ugh. so global token bucket hit 0 and backlog = 28 -> scheduler fallback started preempting based on QoS. That explains the eviction spikes.

ana: (typo) ana: we saw a cost blip from spilled spot evictions — the cloud billing shows 12% more preemptions in us-east1 during the 10m window.

marta: initial triage: rebalancer concurrency is intentionally conservative to avoid thundering drains during AZ-scale events, but here it became the bottleneck.

tyler: proposal: switch to per-pool (per-gpu-pool) token buckets + per-az smoothing window. Means rebalance can proceed concurrently in other pools while one pool is rate-limited. Also add exponential backoff and a short drain_cooldown to avoid two controllers re-draining the same node.

kevin: agree. also add a circuit-breaker metric so we can detect when backlog > 20 and immediately relax limits for 60s. Something like `rebalancer_backlog_override` with admin toggle.

rebalancer-bot: new PR opened by marta: https://github.com/redwood/rebalancer/pull/4123 — implements per-pool buckets + drain_cooldown param. CI passing.

ana: can you add a lightweight canary? maybe roll to eu-west1 first then us-east1. We don't want a runaway if we mis-tuned concurrency.

marta: plan: patch in staging now, run synthetic node-add test (30 node burst) with chaos generator. If stable, canary eu-west1 at 22:00 UTC, then us-east1 at 23:30 UTC. I'll own the rollout and the rollback playbook.

tyler: schedule onboarded, I'll update runbook and dashboards: `rebalancer_backlog`, `rebalancer_throttle_count`, `preemption_rate` with alert thresholds.

kevin: :thumbsup: Also add a cheap GAUGE for `rebalancer_tokens_in_use` so SRE can see saturation in real time.

marta: noted. if anyone sees unexpected evictions during the canary ping @marta immediately.

ana: thanks — and nice catch on the token bucket effect, saved us from a bigger cross-AZ ripple. :heart:

tyler: one more follow-up: should we track cost_delta from rebalancer events in the cost dashboard? put it under infra-costs > solver.

kevin: yes, add a tag `eviction_cause=rebalancer-throttle` to the eviction events so infra-costs can attribute.

marta: I'll include that in the PR.

rebalancer-bot: deploy scheduled to staging at 20:05 UTC.

tyler: great. closing loop here for now.
